_comment: Production sources and trade flows do not always count the same substance, and the
difference is a factor of five for lithium. Flow volumes in this project are carried on
a contained-metal basis, expressed as lithium carbonate equivalent (LCE) for lithium and
rare-earth oxide (REO) for rare earths, so that volume x price produces a sane number.
The USGS reports lithium mine production as contained lithium, not LCE. Comparing the
two directly makes every lithium exporter look like it ships five times what it digs up.
Each factor below converts that source's published figure into the basis flows use.
A mineral with no entry is already on the same basis and needs no conversion.
lithium: 5.323 = the mass ratio of Li2CO3 to Li (73.89 / 13.88). The standard LCE
conversion, published by the USGS itself in the lithium chapter.
The IEA is assumed to publish contained metal on the same basis as the USGS. That is
stated rather than verified, and it only affects a warning threshold, never output.
